system.name: EBS
system.one_liner: Alibaba Cloud's disaggregated elastic block store, whose proxy applies a burst-aware, segment-level token-bucket rate limiter

components.name: Segment 1
components.role: one monitored LBA segment generating I/O requests

components.name: Rate Monitor
components.role: segment-level I/O rate monitor that classifies each segment as hot or steady and tags steady-segment requests

components.name: Tag for steady IO
components.role: marker attached to requests from a segment classified as steady, allowing them to draw from the Cheque Bucket

components.name: Token Update
components.role: periodic process that replenishes tokens in the Main and Cheque Buckets based on estimated available bandwidth

components.name: Main Bucket
components.role: the ordinary token bucket bounding each segment's baseline I/O rate

components.name: Cheque Bucket
components.role: an overdraft token bucket that lets tagged steady segments borrow extra bandwidth during a burst

content.key_idea: A segment-level Rate Monitor tags steady segments; Token Update replenishes a Main Bucket and a Cheque Bucket, letting tagged steady segments borrow extra bandwidth during a burst without starving hot segments or the DFS.
content.reading_order: Left-to-right: Segments 1-3 feed the Rate Monitor, which tags steady IOs; tagged requests plus Token Update drive the Main and Cheque Bucket gauges to produce the rate-limited output.

estimate the available bandwidth to determine how much can be overdrawn

summary: Figure 8 shows EBS's burst-aware rate limiter, which lets steady I/O segments temporarily borrow extra bandwidth during a burst. Segment 1, Segment 2, and Segment 3 send their I/O to a Rate Monitor, which classifies each segment as hot or steady over a fixed interval and attaches a Tag for steady IO to requests from steady segments. Separately, a Token Update process periodically replenishes two token buckets -- a Main Bucket for each segment's baseline allowance and a Cheque Bucket that tagged, steady-segment requests may additionally draw from -- each feeding its own gauge-style rate limiter before requests proceed. The design keeps headroom for the DFS and any hot segments while letting steady segments overdraw during the first window of a burst. The figure is icon-heavy and sparse on text, using color-coded segment tags and coin-stack/gauge icons rather than boxes and labels.
